pr_body: #### What is it? - [x] Bugfix (user facing) - [x] Feature (user facing) #### Description of the changes in your PR Replacement of #7260, rebased with some changes in the feature. This pull request adds the quality selector for livestreams. This quality selector, due to limitations, will only include qualities' resolution (or its bitrate if its height is unknown and as a last resort, the `Quality unknown` string). Contrary to the previous attempt, there is no `Auto` quality, in order to prevent confusion of this availability on videos. The default resolution is set according to the user choices in Video and audio settings. However, resolutions are now set using minimum and maximum video size constraints instead of selection overrides, in order to simply the code. Available resolutions are got from the first video `TrackGroupInfo` found and rebuilt each time the `onTracksChanged(TracksInfo)` event of ExoPlayer is triggered. This PR also refactors how `SourceType`s are used by the player. Instead of being returned only by `VideoPlaybackResolver`, it is now included in `MediaItemTag`s (and the corresponding enum has been extracted from `VideoPlaybackResolver`). This allow detection of sources which require building a quality selector using the first video `TrackGroupInfo` found (like I said above), setting an `AnalyticsListener` to update the quality `TextView` depending of the quality played, and setting the default resolution using `TrackSelectionParameters`. The `SourceType` enum has been changed to contain more values, including a one used for livestreams: `MANIFEST`. As the name suggests, it represents `MediaSource`s generated from a "master" manifest URL. This will allow us in the future to use, if needed, a manifest to play a non-live content with the ability to choose the video quality played (even if a few changes in player and resolver codes will be needed). This enum is now also used to do the seamless transition, instead of the last resolved source, and disabling video and text tracks used for the transition is now always done (so even when the play queue manager is reloaded), in order to fix some blank video issues. Finally, this PR also fixes playability of contents which doesn't have an audio stream and only video streams when trying to play them background (by using `Start playing in the background` or `Enqueue` commands). The default video stream will be played, with potentially text tracks if they are enabled. This is the case on several PeerTube videos. For more detailed changes, please take a look at the code changes. #### Before/After Screenshots/Screen Record - Before: - After: #### Fixes the following issue(s) - Fixes #1239 #### APK testing The APK can be found by going to the "Checks" tab below the title. On the left pane, click on "CI", scroll down to "artifacts" and click "app" to download the zip file which contains the debug APK of this PR. #### Due diligence - [x] I read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
pr_title: Add quality selector for livestreams, fix some seamless transition issues and more

I am closing this PR, as the current player structure doesn't allow us to implement properly this feature.

It we rely directly on ExoPlayer track selection APIs to build quality menus when rewriting the player, we will be able to implement this in a proper way.

For instance, LibreTube uses these APIs for quality selection and has support of this feature.

For other fixes and improvements in this PR, a part of them (or all of them?) have been already done in other PRs and the remaining parts, if any, could be done if needed in the future.

review_comment: Maybe add a small javadoc to this function explaining that the source type on the returned tag is already set to `MANIFEST`, to make it clearer to people reading the code in `Video/AudioPlaybackResolver`.

What is this variable? Why are you setting it to `false` only when Next and Previous are called? Since `setDefaultResolutionForManifestSourcesIfNeeded` does not depend on anything, shouldn't it be called only when `trackSelector` is initialized, i.e. in the `Player` constructor?
Does this make it so that shorts / vertical videos at 1080x1920 are considered high resolution, since 1920>1080?
Are you sure this should be a `>=` and not a `>`? As far as I understand, `MAX_HEIGHT_ALLOWED_WITHOUT_HIGH_RESOLUTIONS` represents the maximum height that is **not** considered a high resolution.
Maybe this could be used also to solve #9103?

Can the "// Create optional audio stream source" lines above be moved into an `if (video == null || video.isVideoOnly())`? I think there is no need to get the audio stream if you already know it's not going to be used
Why do you need to call it again here? It shouldn't make any changes.
Could you add a comment explaining what is happening here?
